paper_metadata.title: Quantum Algorithms for Stochastic Differential Equations: Achieving Polynomial and Super-Polynomial Speedups for High-Dimensional Systems

experiments.description: Quantum amplitude-estimation-based simulation and pricing of multi-asset Black-Scholes basket options, evaluated on small 2- to 4-asset instances and a 2D Black-Scholes example.

algorithm.variant: Amplitude estimation on coherently simulated SDE paths

hyperparameters.assets: 2-4 in numerical examples; d=10 used in resource estimate

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Log-returns encoded into quantum state; additional ancilla used for payoff evaluation; O(d) qubits for asset registers plus O(log(1/epsilon)) qubits for payoff encoding.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate option price C = e^{-rT} E[payoff(S_T)] for a basket of correlated geometric Brownian motion assets.

problem_instance.description: Basket option pricing under multi-asset Black-Scholes / geometric Brownian motion dynamics; includes a 2D correlated-asset example and small 2- to 4-asset instances.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic correlated asset-price dynamics; parameters include drift mu, volatility sigma, correlation matrix, maturity T, and strike K.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Encode log-prices/log-returns on discretized intervals; no empirical dataset preprocessing reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared quantum estimates against analytic Black-Scholes price or high-precision Monte Carlo; reported bias, RMSE, circuit depth, and two-qubit gate count; 8192 shots per circuit; 2- to 4-asset instances and a 2D example.

noise_model.noise_description: Noisy Aer simulation with noise model calibrated to IBM heavy-hex devices

implementation_details.classical_solver: analytic Black-Scholes formula or high-precision Monte Carlo
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Define drift, volatility, correlation matrix, maturity, and strike; build SDE simulation circuit; append payoff encoding block; wrap in amplitude-estimation routine.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Estimate option price and variance; compute bias and RMSE relative to reference price.

speedup_claims.conditions: for expectation estimation via amplitude estimation; accuracy dependence improves from O(1/epsilon^2) to O(1/sqrt(epsilon)) in the paper's claim
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper's asymptotic derivation is internally inconsistent in places (it also states polylog(1/epsilon)); the empirical 2D simulator result reports only about 3x speedup.

speedup_claims.conditions: 2D Black-Scholes simulated example on noisy Aer/Qiskit with 8192 shots
speedup_claims.caveats: Speedup is limited by classical simulation overhead; paper states real-hardware estimate of 10-20x.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(poly(d)/sqrt(epsilon)) oracle complexity for amplitude estimation; overall claimed ˜O(poly(d) polylog(1/epsilon)) in the paper
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: ≈1 second in the 2D classical Monte Carlo comparison

experiments.description: Quantum simulation of Langevin dynamics for coarse-grained molecular systems, including barrier-crossing / hitting-time estimation and rare-event sampling.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid quantum simulation of Langevin dynamics with BAOAB-inspired Trotterized ansatz and amplitude estimation for hitting-time observables
algorithm.ansatz: Trotterized BAOAB splitting with drift, noise, and symplectic mixer blocks
algorithm.num_layers: L = O(log d) for most experiments

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Registers allocated for each pair (q_i, v_i) plus ancillae; coarse-grained coordinates and velocities are encoded into qubit registers.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the probability of crossing a barrier within time T, i.e., a hitting-time / rare-event probability for Langevin dynamics.

problem_instance.description: Protein coarse-grained Langevin dynamics example with 3 beads; barrier-crossing probability / rare-event sampling.

dataset_specification.description: Coarse-grained molecular system with collective coordinates q and velocities v; potential U(q), friction gamma, and thermal noise term.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No dataset preprocessing reported; model is a synthetic coarse-grained molecular dynamics setup.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared quantum estimates to classical Brownian-dynamics simulations using the BAOAB integrator; reported smaller RMSE for fixed wall-clock budget on simulator and ~100x speedup claim for rare-event sampling.

noise_model.noise_description: Noisy Aer simulation with noise model calibrated to IBM heavy-hex devices

implementation_details.classical_solver: classical Brownian-dynamics simulation using BAOAB integrator
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct coarse-grained Langevin model; encode coordinate and velocity registers; build drift/noise/symplectic mixer layers.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Estimate barrier-crossing probability / hitting-time indicator and compare RMSE against classical simulation.

classical_baselines.method_name: classical brownian-dynamics simulation using baoab integrator

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical brownian-dynamics simulation using BAOAB integrator
speedup_claims.conditions: rare-event sampling / barrier-crossing probability estimation for a 3-bead coarse-grained Langevin system
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports this as an approximate speedup claim; no exact RMSE numbers are provided.
Theoretical claim; no detailed benchmark table for this experiment.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: ˜O(poly(d)) per trajectory; amplitude-estimation overhead gives quadratic improvement in sampling
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: ˜O(poly(d)) per sample; Monte Carlo sampling scales as O(1/epsilon^2) for expectation estimation

experiments.description: Variational quantum scheme for nonlinear SDEs using a problem-informed parameterized circuit to approximate the SDE solution operator.

algorithm.variant: Problem-informed variational quantum ansatz for nonlinear SDEs with layer-wise training
algorithm.ansatz: Parameterized circuit U(theta) with data encoding, drift approximation, noise injection, and output measurement layers
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial parameters chosen close to classical values; avoids random initialization in a large parameter space

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Initial distribution encoded via Ry(theta_0^(i)) layers; drift and noise represented by shallow unitary blocks and parameterized random unitaries.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize L(theta) = sum_i (E_quantum[f_i(X_i)] - E_classical[f_i(X_i)])^2 over test observables.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Layer-wise training and local cost functions to mitigate barren plateaus; no explicit penalty formulation reported.

problem_instance.description: General nonlinear SDEs where exact Hamiltonian simulation is infeasible; no single benchmark instance specified.

dataset_specification.description: Abstract nonlinear SDE setting with Lipschitz drift and noise terms; observables are test functions f_i.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical training/error analysis only; no concrete numerical benchmark details beyond the general framework.

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: Layer-wise training, local cost functions, shallow circuits to mitigate barren plateaus and noise sensitivity
noise_model.mitigation_details: Problem-informed ansatz; shallow depth; layer-wise optimization; local observables
noise_model.noise_description: Hardware noise included in the a priori error bound as a term proportional to hardware noise · L

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct test functions and initialize parameters near classical values.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare quantum and classical observable estimates in the loss function.

speedup_claims.conditions: nonlinear SDEs with problem-informed ansatz, shallow depth L = O(log d), and layer-wise training
speedup_claims.caveats: No numerical benchmark or runtime comparison is reported; only a priori error scaling is given.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Polynomial in d with p trainable parameters and depth L = O(log d); approximation error O(1/sqrt(p) + hardware noise · L)

experiments.description: Theoretical Schrödingerization-based quantum simulation of the Fokker-Planck equation associated with an SDE.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Discretized Fokker-Planck operator on a d-dimensional grid; state dimension N_x = n_s^d and qubit count log N_x = d log n_s.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Simulate the Fokker-Planck PDE ∂_t p = L p via a self-adjoint transformed operator H and recover p(t,x) from u(t,x) = w(x)p(t,x).
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H obtained by conjugating the Fokker-Planck operator with a weighting function w(x) to form a self-adjoint operator.

problem_instance.description: Generic Fokker-Planck equation associated with an SDE; no concrete market or molecular dataset.

dataset_specification.description: d-dimensional spatial grid with n_s points per dimension; finite-difference stencil yields O(d) non-zero entries per row.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No empirical preprocessing; discretization and weighting transformation only.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical complexity comparison against classical finite-difference solvers.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize the PDE on a d-dimensional grid.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Recover density p(t,x) from transformed state u(t,x).

speedup_claims.conditions: d-dimensional Fokker-Planck equation discretized on an n_s^d grid; quantum query complexity claimed as ~O(d T polylog(N_x, 1/epsilon)) and stated as ~O(d log(1/epsilon)) under the paper's assumptions
speedup_claims.caveats: Purely theoretical; no numerical experiment is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: ˜O(d T polylog(N_x, 1/epsilon)) query complexity; stated as ˜O(d log(1/epsilon)) under the paper's discretization assumptions
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(n_s^d) space and O(n_s^(d+1)) time; under comparable accuracy constraints, O(epsilon^(-d-1)) scaling
